\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{عذرخواهی} \fa{کردن} ('ozrkhâhi kardan)}{عذرخواهی کردن ('ozrkhâhi kardan)}]{\fa{عذرخواهی} \fa{کردن} ('ozrkhâhi kardan) — to apologize}

\label{lesson:FA-C442-ozrkhahi-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to back down, then the Persian for dissatisfied.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{عذرخواهی} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{عذرخواهی} \fa{کردن}} (\emph{'ozrkhâhi kardan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to apologize\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{مدیر} \fa{هتل} \fa{از} \fa{ما} \fa{عذرخواهی} \fa{کرد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Modir-e hotel az mâ 'ozrkhâhi kard.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The hotel manager apologized to us.
\end{quote}

\emph{'ozr} 'excuse' + \emph{khâh} 'asking' + \emph{-i} + \emph{kardan}. Note the letter \fa{ذ}, said \emph{z}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{'ozrkhâhi kardan} is built from \emph{'ozr} 'an excuse', a loan usually traced to Arabic \emph{ʿuḏr}, native \emph{khâh}, the present stem of \emph{khâstan} 'to ask, to want', and \emph{kardan} 'to do'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{'ozrkhâhi kardan}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{'ozrkhâhi kardan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{'ozrkhâhi kardan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to back down, then the Persian for dissatisfied, then say \emph{'ozrkhâhi kardan} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \fa{عذرخواهی} \fa{کردن} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To apologize\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{جبران} \fa{کردن} (jobrân kardan)}{جبران کردن (jobrân kardan)}]{\fa{جبران} \fa{کردن} (jobrân kardan) — to make up for, to make amends for}

\label{lesson:FA-C442-jobran-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for dissatisfied, then the Persian for to apologize.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{جبران} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{جبران} \fa{کردن}} (\emph{jobrân kardan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to make up for, to make amends for\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{هتل} \fa{اشتباهش} \fa{را} \fa{با} \fa{یک} \fa{شب} \fa{مجانی} \fa{جبران} \fa{کرد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Hotel eshtebâhash râ bâ yek shab-e majâni jobrân kard.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The hotel made up for its mistake with a free night.
\end{quote}

Also to repay a kindness: \emph{lotf-e shomâ râ jobrân mikonam}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{jobrân kardan} is built from \emph{jobrân} 'compensation', a loan usually traced to Arabic \emph{jubrān} 'mending, setting right', and \emph{kardan} 'to do'. EtymDB does not list \emph{jobrân}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jobrân kardan}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jobrân kardan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{jobrân kardan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for dissatisfied, then the Persian for to apologize, then say \emph{jobrân kardan} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \fa{جبران} \fa{کردن} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To make up for, to make amends for\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{تعویض} \fa{کردن} (ta'viz kardan)}{تعویض کردن (ta'viz kardan)}]{\fa{تعویض} \fa{کردن} (ta'viz kardan) — to exchange, to replace}

\label{lesson:FA-C442-taviz-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to apologize, then the Persian for to make up for.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{تعویض} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{تعویض} \fa{کردن}} (\emph{ta'viz kardan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to exchange, to replace\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{فروشگاه} \fa{کفش} \fa{پاره} \fa{را} \fa{تعویض} \fa{کرد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Forushgâh kafsh-e pâre râ ta'viz kard.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The shop exchanged the torn shoes.
\end{quote}

More formal than \emph{'avaz kardan}. Note the letter \fa{ض}, said \emph{z}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{ta'viz kardan} is built from \emph{ta'viz} 'replacement', a loan usually traced to Arabic \emph{taʿwīḍ} 'replacing, compensating', and \emph{kardan} 'to do'. EtymDB does not list \emph{ta'viz}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{ta'viz kardan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to apologize, then the Persian for to make up for, then say \emph{ta'viz kardan} again

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{پس} \fa{گرفتن} (pas gereftan)}{پس گرفتن (pas gereftan)}]{\fa{پس} \fa{گرفتن} (pas gereftan) — to take back; to get back (money)}

\label{lesson:FA-C442-pas-gereftan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to make up for, then the Persian for to exchange.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{پس} \fa{گرفتن}}
\textbf{\fa{پس} \fa{گرفتن}} (\emph{pas gereftan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to take back; to get back (money)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{پول} \fa{بلیت} \fa{را} \fa{پس} \fa{گرفتیم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Pul-e bilit râ pas gereftim.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
We got the ticket money back.
\end{quote}

\emph{pas} 'back' + \emph{gereftan}. The opposite of \emph{pas dâdan} 'to give back'.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{pas gereftan} is built from \emph{pas} 'back, behind', inherited from Middle Persian \emph{pas} (EtymDB), and the native verb \emph{gereftan} 'to take', usually traced to Old Persian \emph{grab-}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pas gereftan}, once more

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to make up for, then the Persian for to exchange, then say \emph{pas gereftan} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{برگرداندن} (bargardândan)}{برگرداندن (bargardândan)}]{\fa{برگرداندن} (bargardândan) — to give back, to return (something)}

\label{lesson:FA-C442-bargardandan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to exchange, then the Persian for to take back.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{برگرداندن}}
\textbf{\fa{برگرداندن}} (\emph{bargardândan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to give back, to return (something)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{فروشنده} \fa{پول} \fa{ما} \fa{را} \fa{برگرداند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Forushande pul-e mâ râ bargardând.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The shopkeeper gave our money back.
\end{quote}

The causative of \emph{bargashtan} 'to go back'. Present stem \emph{bargardân-}: \emph{barmigardânam}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{bargardândan} is built from \emph{bar} 'up, back' and \emph{gardândan} 'to turn something', the causative built on \emph{gard-}, the present stem of \emph{gashtan} 'to turn', usually traced to Middle Persian \emph{gaštan}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
